scientific_question: Can an auditable, state-aware, permutation-invariant mixture representation transfer experimental conductivity knowledge from previously measured lithium-salt systems to a completely held-out LiAsF6 system, and does it beat state-only, chemistry-destroyed, wrong-salt, and same-label-budget target-only alternatives?

eligibility.source_filter: conductivity_mask is true and conductivity is finite and positive
eligibility.anchor_test_exclusion: Every record sharing an exact formulation with an anchor is excluded from scoring

representation.molecule: Ten scaled physicochemical descriptors, eleven element fractions, and a 256-bit radius-2 Morgan fingerprint
representation.mixture: Normalized-molar-weight solvent mean and variance plus normalized-molar-weight salt mean

few_shot_adapter.type: zero-prior ridge correction of the frozen donor prediction

primary_interpretation.knowledge_contribution: The full source model must improve both log-RMSE and Spearman correlation over the state-only and chemistry-permuted controls.
primary_interpretation.data_poor_rescue: At five target anchors, the frozen source prediction or its shrinkage adapter must improve log-RMSE over the strongest same-anchor target-only baseline.
primary_interpretation.routing: If calibration does not improve but ranking remains materially positive, route the edge to candidate ordering rather than numerical prediction.
primary_interpretation.negative_transfer: If the full source model loses to its controls or the target-only baseline, reject the edge.

claim_guard: This analysis was designed after the 2026 LiAsF6 outcomes and published transfer results were inspected. It is method development and retrospective external benchmarking, not prospective confirmation. It may justify freezing the representation and routing rule for an independent electrolyte programme, but it cannot by itself establish a new confirmatory edge or laboratory discovery acceleration.
